title: Two written numerals between 1 and 10
keyIdea: Compare two written numerals from 1 to 10 by their value: which is greater, which is less. How tall the digit looks does not change the number.
familyTip: Flash two number cards (1–10). Ask 'Which is more?' then 'Which is less?' Point along a 1–10 line so greater sits further right.

visual.caption: Greater, less, or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: 9 sits near the right on a 1–10 line
a taller drawn 1 beats a tiny 9

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap greater and less, place on a 1–10 line, use greater/less words, reject look-not-value, build a greater left, then challenge.

kid: Two numbers on cards mean amounts.
The greater number means more. The less number means fewer.
On a line from 1 to 10, bigger numbers sit further right.
How fat or tall a digit looks does not change its value.
adult: CCSS K.CC.C.7 / EYFS number: compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals. Words: greater, less, more, fewer, numeral, value.
Common mistakes: judging by how large the digit is drawn; mixing up left/right on the number line; saying same-looking sizes are equal when values differ; reading the first card as always greater.
In the lab your child taps the greater and lesser numeral, places 9 on a 1–10 line, fills greater/less language, rejects look-not-value myths, and raises a left numeral past a right one.

practice.hint: Greater means the numeral that stands for more ones.
practice.explain: 7 is greater than 3 because seven ones beat three ones.

practice.hint: Less means the numeral that stands for fewer ones.
practice.explain: 2 is less than 8 — two ones are fewer than eight ones.

practice.prompt: Which is greater: {a} or {b}? Type the greater one.
practice.hint: The second number sits in the higher band — type that greater numeral.
practice.explain: Between {a} and {b}, the greater value is {b}.

practice.prompt: Which is less: {a} or {b}? Type the lesser one.
practice.hint: The first number sits in the lower band — type that lesser numeral.
practice.explain: Between {a} and {b}, the lesser value is {a}.

practice.prompt: Order the steps to compare two written numerals.
practice.hint: Read both written numbers carefully before you decide.
practice.explain: Compare values first, then name greater or less — ignore how tall the digit looks.

pool.hint: Greater numbers sit further toward the right end of the line.
pool.explain: 9 is near the right end because it is one of the greater values.

pool.hint: Four ones compared with nine ones — which side has fewer?

pool.prompt: Huge drawn 1 vs tiny drawn 9 — greater is…
pool.hint: Ignore drawing size; compare the numeral values themselves.
pool.explain: 9 is greater even if 1 is drawn huge — value wins.

pool.hint: Equal numeral values match; they are not greater or less.
pool.explain: Same numeral value means they are the same, not greater or less.

pool.hint: Type the larger written value — here it is the second numeral.
Type the smaller written value — here it is the first numeral.

pool.prompt: Why ignore how fat a digit looks?
pool.hint: Drawing style is not what decides greater or less.
pool.explain: Only the numeral's value matters when you compare written numbers.

pool.prompt: Order: place a numeral on a 1–10 line.
pool.hint: Start near 1 on the left and move right as values grow.
pool.explain: The line grows rightward; greater numerals sit further along.
